decisions.executionNote: Begin gradual elbow-up-compatible reorientation toward top-down grasps; table and fingertip offsets estimated visually.
Align above the nearer chocolate and green car with vertical grippers. Bars and toys will need center staging to respect arm workspaces.
Turn closing axes across narrow object dimensions while lowering cautiously toward pregrasp height.
Fine-align and lower to grasp the gold chocolate wrapper and green car, then close; retention must be checked on lift.
Stop downward motion at observed contact height, allow closure, then perform a short retention-check lift.
Both objects visibly retained. Lift clear, carry green car toward middle basket, and stage chocolate at the center boundary for the right arm.
Replan with smaller translations after IK continuity rejection; lower left chocolate to center staging and approach blue basket with the retained car.
Car appears to have slipped; retreat right for a fresh grasp. Continue placing chocolate at the center boundary without crossing arms.
Release chocolate at the midline for later right-arm pickup; withdraw left and align right above the slipped green car.
Regrasp green car near basket edge while left approaches the remaining diagonal chocolate bar.
Lower left toward remaining bar; test right-car retention with a slow vertical lift before transferring.
Correct white-bar centering before closing. Green car was not retained; approach its front half to avoid basket-rim interference.
Reduce right-arm increments after zero-step IK rejection; continue white-bar centering and closure.
Lift white chocolate for retention check; attempt a lower nose grasp on green car away from basket walls.
White bar was not retained; retry slightly deeper and centered. Lift green car backward away from the rim to check its grasp.
Close white-bar grasp at contact height and lift slowly. Recenter the green-car grasp with vertical fingers and narrower approach opening to clear the basket rim.
Retry white chocolate at a lower grasp depth, and shift right toward the visible green-car body before closure; prior lifts showed no retention.
Allow complete closure at the latest contact poses before a very short lift; verify object retention visually.
Correct left gripper's horizontal fingertip offset and verticality; switch right to the unobstructed yellow car rather than repeatedly contacting the basket rim.
Correct malformed rotation entry; same intended open-jaw pregrasp centering, from unchanged observation.
Center objects between jaws using the new wrist views, descend slightly, and close both for a controlled grasp test.
Let both grippers finish closing, then lift only four centimeters to assess retention.
Move the yellow-car body toward the actual fingertip line, and realign white chocolate after it rotated during the failed closure.
Try a deeper yellow-car grasp; recenter white bar and align jaws normal to its new long axis before closing.
Hold closure at observed contact poses, then make a short vertical lift to verify both grasps.
Both objects appear retained in the short lift. Raise clear of the tabletop while keeping jaws closed and moving gently inward.
Carry retained yellow car toward the middle basket; bring white chocolate to a separate center staging area without crossing arms.
Unwind left wrist away from its angle wrap while lowering to staging. Continue car transfer with smaller increments and a slight height reduction for reach margin.
Lower and modestly tilt right wrist to improve reach margin toward blue basket after continuity interruption; complete left-side staging approach.
Release white chocolate at the center staging area and withdraw left. Move the tilted yellow car over the blue-basket interior before opening.
Yellow car is over the blue basket; open and retreat right with reach margin. Clear left arm from the staged chocolates.
Yellow car visibly rests inside blue basket. Retreat with smaller right increments after IK rejection and clear the center transfer area.
Approach staged gold chocolate from the right side of the center boundary; keep left arm clear and rotate right jaws across the wrapper.
Refine staged-chocolate pickup with a slight inward fingertip tilt while keeping the right EE on its own side; avoid the nearby wooden toy.
Allow chocolate grasp to settle, then lift clear of the nearby toy to verify that only the wrapper is retained.
Chocolate was not retained. Clear the interfering wooden toy first with a centered body grasp, for transfer to the left arm.
Settle the wooden-toy grasp and test a vertical lift before moving it to center staging.
Toy was not retained. Retry at lower body-grasp height while keeping the same planar alignment and the left arm clear.
Hold closure at the deeper wooden-toy grasp, then lift slowly to distinguish retention from tabletop contact.
Wooden toy now visibly follows the lift. Carry it to a clear center staging spot for pickup by the left arm.
Lower the retained wooden toy onto the clear midline staging spot and release for a left-arm pickup.
Withdraw right clear of the released toy before approaching it from the left; keep separated midline approach paths.
Lower left onto the staged wooden toy; right approaches the now-clear gold chocolate with corrected lateral jaw alignment.
Close left around the staged toy. Lower and tilt right fingertips toward the gold bar center before closing, keeping both EEs on their own sides.
Settle both closures, then lift and gently separate the arms to check retention of the toy and gold chocolate.
Both objects remain visible at the jaws. Carry wooden toy toward the white basket and gold chocolate toward the red basket, maintaining clearance and closed jaws.
Toy slipped onto the table; return left for a body grasp. Continue retained chocolate over the red basket with slight forward wrist tilt for reach margin.
Release gold chocolate into the red basket and withdraw. Recenter left over the fallen toy's belly rather than its legs and lower for a firmer body grasp.
Close left on the toy body and test a small lift. Approach the remaining white chocolate with the right arm while leaving the gold bar in its assigned basket.
Move the retained wooden toy slowly toward the white basket. Refine and close the right-arm grasp on the staged white chocolate.
Toy slipped again; rotate the left closing axis across its body rather than the legs. Recenter white chocolate between the right jaws and retry closure.
Settle and lift white chocolate. Bring the left jaws onto the toy body after reorientation, keeping wrist rotation away from its wrap boundary.
Neither grasp is secure. Clear left from rim contact and recenter; straighten right fingers for a deeper, parallel-sided grasp on the thin white bar.
Align right jaws perpendicular to the white wrapper's diagonal axis at low grasp height. Approach the left toy's body from behind the rim.
Allow complete closure at the observed contact poses, then lift both objects slightly to verify retention before carrying.
White chocolate is retained; carry it toward the right basket. Retry left toy with deeper body alignment and an opening direction that avoids the basket wall.
Close the left toy grasp at the observed contact pose. Carry retained white chocolate over the red basket with a small forward wrist tilt for reach margin.
Release white chocolate beside the gold bar in the red basket and retreat right. Lift and gently carry the broader left toy grasp toward the white basket.
Both chocolates are visibly in the red basket. Retry the slipped wooden toy nearer its head; approach the upright green car high with reduced jaw opening to avoid basket-wall contact.
Replan after the one-step continuity interruption using smaller right rotation and translation increments; continue separate toy and car approaches.
Center the left grasp deeper on the toy body away from the rim. Finish aligning the right closing axis across the upright green car.
Align right on the upright green car's thin body. Reorient left jaws parallel to the basket front to avoid wall contact during toy closure.
Replan from observed contact poses: clear left away from the basket before further rotation. Close right on the green car and test a small backward extraction.
Approach the left toy with vertical fingers opening parallel to the basket front. Retry a narrow nose grasp on the green car below its previous missed contact.
Make small depth and centering corrections for the toy body and the green-car nose, then close both. Prior right closure was empty.
Extract left slowly backward from rim contact to test retention. Clear right behind the basket front before a deeper car-nose approach.
Toy follows the backward lift; carry it gently above the white basket. Close the deeper right car grasp and test a short extraction.
Place the retained wooden toy inside the white basket and withdraw left. Clear right from the unsuccessful car grip toward the remaining wooden toy.
First wooden toy is visibly inside the white basket. Center and close the right gripper on the remaining toy while left withdraws for the next staged transfer.
Settle the remaining wooden-toy grasp and verify retention with a short lift; position left at a separated receiving approach.
Carry the retained second wooden toy to the clear midline staging area, keeping left withdrawn for an uncrossed transfer.
Set the second wooden toy onto the midline, release, and begin separating the arms for left pickup.
Approach staged second toy from the left with a slight inward fingertip tilt. Withdraw right toward a fresh vertical approach to the green car.
Use an inward fingertip tilt to reach the staged toy without crossing arm workspaces; advance the right narrow jaws onto the upright car's exposed nose.
Close both refined grasps and make only short retention checks: vertical lift for the toy and backward extraction for the car.
Test the left toy retention gently. Lower right fingertips toward the green car's low exposed nose, correcting the planar offset and avoiding the basket front.
Carry the retained second toy toward the white basket while straightening the wrist. Close on the exposed car nose and make a slow backward-upward extraction.
Green car is retained by its nose; lift and carry it slowly toward the blue basket. Regrasp the second toy now on the left tabletop with vertical jaws.
Replan smaller right motions after the continuity stop, tilting forward for basket reach. Center and close left deeper on the remaining toy body.
